threads.body: This helper inserts hoplology rows through `db.get()`, whose production connections have `PRAGMA query_only=ON`; every insert therefore fails and the watcher records zero inserts as success. Use the writer pool and propagate pool/insert failures so the file remains eligible for retry.

The dedup state is updated before persistence succeeds. If writer checkout or the insert fails, the paired target-only line is then treated as a duplicate, so both phrasings can produce no database row. Update `last_rez_dedup` only after a successful persist.

The only writer connection is acquired before the file is read and parsed, so a large daily log blocks live ingestion for the entire parse rather than only the insert transaction. Parse and collect the arena matches first, then check out the writer around the inserts/commit as the PR’s startup-backfill design requires.

This issue also appears on line 425 of the same file.

This checkout occurs before the `BufReader` loop, so the sole writer remains occupied during all file I/O and parsing. That prevents live writers from interleaving during a large file; collect the parsed wisdom records first and acquire the writer only for persistence.

The writer checkout still precedes the complete line-reading/parsing loop, monopolizing the single-writer queue for each file. Parse roulette results before checkout and keep only the insert/commit phase inside the writer transaction.

The sole writer is held while every chat line is read and parsed, despite the stated parse-before-checkout design. On a large log this stalls live ingest for the whole file; collect words used first, then acquire the writer for the delete transaction.

The date toolbar is rendered before a channel is selected, and this function omits the channel filter when `selectedChannel` is null. Selecting a day then fills the “Select a Channel” view with messages from every channel. Guard this loader until a channel has been selected.
